title: Star trails over Paranal
caption: Star trails over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Star trails form an archway over ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory, high in the Chilean desert. The telescopes below stand still while the sky seems to wheel above them.

The VLT is not a single instrument. It is made up of four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes and four 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes. Together they share this high desert site, and the photograph gathers all of them under a single sweep of sky.

The arch of trails comes from Earth's rotation. During a long exposure, the camera turns with the planet, and each star traces a curve across the image. Only the sky appears to move, because everything on the ground, including the telescopes, is turning along with the camera. The result compresses a stretch of the night into one frame.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only a long exposure can record their apparent motion as arcs.

explore: The pattern of star trails changes with the direction the camera faces. Near a celestial pole they curl into circles, while elsewhere they form long arcs like these.
alt: Star trails forming an arch across the night sky above the telescope enclosures of the Very Large Telescope.
